question.text: What percentage of the EU hen flock will be sexed with in-ovo sexing technology in Q1 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the percentage of the EU's commercial layer hen flock that was sexed with in-ovo technology according to official the first such non-preliminary number published by Innovate Animal Ag in 2027.
question.fine_print: If Innovate Animal Ag does not publish any such number in 2027 or if the criteria are significantly changed such that previous reporting is not comparable, this question can be resolved by another credible source if it is comparable. Otherwise the question will be **annulled**.

research:
I've finished the research and am writing up the findings now.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-07 (page says "Updated July 2026"): Innovate Animal Ag's current market-penetration page puts the EU at **40%** of the commercial layer flock sexed in-ovo **as of June 1, 2026**, with a range of 36.2-43.3%. That is 125-142M sexed hens out of a commercial flock of 328-346M, or 371-388M if about 42M backyard hens are added. The same page revises earlier years upward: April 2024 from 20% to **23%**, and April 2025 from 28% to **34%**, because the flock-size estimate was refined. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- The page's forecast is about **51% by July 2028** (range 47-55%), driven partly by Italy's ban from January 2027. It gives no figure for 2027. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- Timing of the reports: the 2025 report came out in May 2025 with end-of-Q1 data. The 2026 report came out in July 2026 with June 1 data. So the 2027 report's snapshot date may not fall in Q1, and it may be published after the expected resolution date of 2027-05-31. [IAA 2025 recap](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-2025-review)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The 2027 figure has not been published. The latest official value is 40% (June 2026). That is already above the question's anchor of 28% and close to the middle of its 20-50 range.
- A comparability issue: the background's 28% belongs to the old flock basis of 393M hens. Under the new basis (about 334M commercial hens), the same period is 34%. Future reports will probably use the new basis.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: News reports say the Commission's 2027 work programme leaves out a ban on cages for sows. I found nothing in it about chick culling. [Corriere](https://www.corriere.it/animali/26_novembre_04/stop-alle-gabbie-negli-allevamenti-l-ue-continua-a-fare-melina-salta-ancora-la-legge-per-tutelare-le-scrofe-77a81a0e-f3fb-4c59-8d8b-5bdc3d353xlk.shtml)
- 2026-11-03: H5N1 outbreaks are leading to housing orders in Germany. Culls could change flock size and the ratio of sexed to total hens. [topagrar](https://www.topagrar.com/gefluegel/schleswig-holstein-verhangt-landesweite-schutzmassnahmen-drei-vogelgrippefallen-d-20030581.html)
- 2026-10-05: IAA's Q3 roundup restates the EU at 40% and says it will pass 50% by 2028. Global capacity is about 100M female chicks per year. In September, Italian Senate amendments proposed €5-10M a year to fund hatchery equipment; similar proposals failed earlier. Minister Lollobrigida points to the Food Sovereignty Fund instead. In July, the EU Livestock Strategy said the Commission intends to propose ending chick culling across the EU by the end of 2026, with no timeline. [IAA Q3 2026](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q3-2026)
- 2026-09-09: AgFunder reports 40% EU penetration. It asks whether Italian producers will import day-old chicks instead of sexing locally. [AgFunder](https://agfundernews.com/in-ovo-sexing-hits-40-penetration-in-the-eu-what-will-it-take-to-crack-the-us)
- Italy's ban applies from 2027-01-01, and its guidelines require in-ovo sexing. The country culls roughly 30-35M male chicks a year. [Il Sole 24 Ore](https://en.ilsole24ore.com/art/male-chicks-killed-birth-ready-guidelines-stop-2027-AHKkAif), [Eurogroup](https://www.eurogroupforanimals.org/node/5614)

## 4. Base rates
- Figures as first published: about 15% (2023 report) [AgFunder](https://agfundernews.com/in-ovo-sexing-reaches-15-penetration-in-eu-as-tech-to-end-male-chick-culling-advances), 20% (March 2024), 28% (end of Q1 2025, range 26-30%) [Poultry World](https://poultryworld.net/the-industrymarkets/market-trends-analysis-the-industrymarkets-2/in-ovo-sexing-gaining-traction), 40% (June 2026).
- Revised series: 23% (April 2024), then 34% (April 2025, +11 points), then 40% (June 2026, +6 points over 14 months). Growth is slowing: about 5 points a year most recently.
- IAA's path to 51% by July 2028 works out to about +5.5 points a year. Simple interpolation gives roughly 43-45% around Q1 to mid-2027. That is my arithmetic, not an IAA number.
- Revisions so far have gone upward by 3-6 points, and the published uncertainty band is about ±3.5 points.
- Each bird lives about 80 weeks, so hatchery adoption shows up in flock share with a lag. Italy's ban mainly lifts the share from 2027 to 2028, over about 18 months.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the supplied Kalshi or Polymarket markets match this question. They cover Flock cameras, the EU budget, tariffs and similar topics. I found no Manifold or Metaculus market on EU in-ovo penetration.
- The only expert forecast is IAA's own: about 51% by July 2028 (range 47-55%).

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2027-01-01: Italy's ban takes effect. Watch for extensions, subsidy decisions, and whether producers rely on imported sexed chicks.
- By the end of 2026: a possible Commission proposal to end chick culling across the EU. It is not mentioned in the 2027 work programme coverage I found.
- About early January 2027: IAA's 2026 year-in-review. About early April 2027: its Q1 2027 roundup. Both could repeat or update the figures.
- About May-July 2027: the likely 2027 IAA penetration report. Its snapshot date (April or June) and any further revision to flock size are the main risks for resolution and comparability.
- Winter 2026-27: avian influenza culls affecting the size of the EU flock.

I could not find any interim 2027 estimate, or any statement about when the next report will be published.

Sources: [IAA forecast](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast), [IAA Q3 2026](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q3-2026), [IAA 2025 recap](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-2025-review), [IAA Q2 2025](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q2-2025), [AgFunder 2026](https://agfundernews.com/in-ovo-sexing-hits-40-penetration-in-the-eu-what-will-it-take-to-crack-the-us), [HumanProgress](https://humanprogress.org/in-ovo-sexing-market-penetration-and-forecast-innovate-animal-ag/), [Poultry World](https://poultryworld.net/the-industrymarkets/market-trends-analysis-the-industrymarkets-2/in-ovo-sexing-gaining-traction), [Il Sole 24 Ore](https://en.ilsole24ore.com/art/male-chicks-killed-birth-ready-guidelines-stop-2027-AHKkAif), [Eurogroup](https://www.eurogroupforanimals.org/node/5614)

## 1. Resolution source

- 2026-07 (page marked "Updated July 2026"): Innovate Animal Ag's [Market Penetration and Forecast](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast) page says **40% of the EU commercial layer flock** was sexed in-ovo as of **June 1, 2026**. The range is 36.2% to 43.3%. The denominator is about 328.7 to 346.0 million hens (401 million registered hen places, at 81.9% to 86% utilization). Suppliers (AAT, Nectra, Orbem, Omegga, Seleggt) reported the hens they sexed from Dec 1, 2024 to May 31, 2026, an 18-month laying cycle. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- The same report revised the April 1, 2025 figure **up from 28% to 34%** because it used a smaller flock estimate. It also revised April 1, 2024 from 20% to 23%. The 28% in the question background is the old, superseded figure. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- Timing: the 2025 report (Q1 2025 data) came out 2025-05-15. The 2026 report used June 1 data and came out in July 2026. If the 2027 report follows the 2026 pattern, it may measure a date after Q1 and may appear after the 2027-05-31 resolution date. That could cause a timing mismatch with the question's "Q1 2027" wording. [IAA blog](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog), [HumanProgress, 2026-07-23](https://humanprogress.org/in-ovo-sexing-market-penetration-and-forecast-innovate-animal-ag/)

## 2. Current status

- Nothing has settled the question yet. No 2027 figure exists. The latest official value is 40% (June 1, 2026).

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

- 2026-11-04: The Commission's 2027 work programme reportedly does not mention the laying hen, broiler and pig welfare revisions. One commentator thinks the poultry proposal (cage phase-out and an end to chick culling) may still come out in December 2026. I could not check the official text. [vegan-news](https://www.vegan-news.net/the-commissions-new-work-programme-where-are-the-animals), [Corriere](https://www.corriere.it/animali/26_novembre_04/stop-alle-gabbie-negli-allevamenti-l-ue-continua-a-fare-melina-salta-ancora-la-legge-per-tutelare-le-scrofe-77a81a0e-f3fb-4c59-8d8b-5bdc3d353xlk.shtml)
- 2026-11-03: Germany and other countries reported H5N1 outbreaks and indoor-housing orders. Bird flu culls could shift both the flock denominator and restocking. [topagrar](https://www.topagrar.com/gefluegel/schleswig-holstein-verhangt-landesweite-schutzmassnahmen-drei-vogelgrippefallen-d-20030581.html)
- 2026-10-05: IAA's Q3 roundup repeats 40% and says the EU should pass 50% by 2028. Other points:
  - Lohmann Deutschland sexes 95% of its conventional chicks and 80% of its organic chicks in-ovo.
  - A new AAT Cheggy machine went live at Novoponte in France in July 2026.
  - Italy's ban starts at the end of 2026. Senate amendments for €5 to 10 million a year in hatchery funding are pending, and similar proposals failed before.
  
  [IAA Q3 2026](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q3-2026)
- 2026-09-09: AgFunderNews reports the 40% figure. Omegga/CET's hyperspectral system is due to launch in late 2026 or early 2027. [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/in-ovo-sexing-hits-40-penetration-in-the-eu-what-will-it-take-to-crack-the-us)
- 2026-07: The EU Livestock Strategy commits to a poultry welfare revision, including an end to chick culling, by the end of 2026. These are plans, not legal deadlines. [EC Food Safety](https://food.ec.europa.eu/animals/animal-welfare/evaluations-and-impact-assessment/revision-eu-animal-welfare-legislation_en), [ALI](https://ali.ong/en/updates/the-eu-livestock-strategy/)
- Italy: the ban on culling male chicks applies from 31 Dec 2026 / 1 Jan 2027. I found no confirmed postponement. Because flocks turn over every ~18 months, IAA expects the ban to raise penetration gradually rather than all at once. [greenMe](https://www.greenme.it/animali/allevamenti/stop-alla-strage-dei-pulcini-maschi-in-italia-finalmente-entra-in-vigore-il-divieto-ecco-quando/), [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)

## 4. Base rates and trend

Official series, as revised in 2026:

- 2024-04-01: 23%
- 2025-04-01: 34% (up 11 points in a year)
- 2026-06-01: 40% (up 6 points in 14 months, about 5 points a year)

Other reference points:

- Earlier published figures, before revision: about 15% (2023), 20% (2024), 28% (Q1 2025). [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/in-ovo-sexing-reaches-15-penetration-in-eu-as-tech-to-end-male-chick-culling-advances), [IAA blog](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-has-now-hit-20-of-the-market-in-the-eu)
- IAA's base forecast is about 51% by July 2028 (range 47% to 55%). A straight line from 40% in June 2026 to 51% in July 2028 is about 0.44 points a month. That implies roughly 44% for April 2027 and roughly 45% for June 2027. This is my arithmetic, not an IAA number. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- Growth has slowed: annual gains fell from 11 points to about 5 points.
- Revision risk is large. Last year a denominator change moved the figure by 6 points (28% to 34%). Each new report's uncertainty band is about ±3.5 points.
- Production in Europe now exceeds 8 million female chicks a month (over 100 million a year). In the 12 months to June 2026 it was more than 92 million. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)

## 5. Other forecasts

- I found no prediction market (Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold) or Metaculus question on this. None of the markets supplied are relevant: they cover Flock cameras, the EU budget, tariffs and similar.
- The only expert forecast I found is IAA's own: about 51% by July 2028 (47% to 55%) and "pass 50% by 2028." [IAA Q3 2026](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q3-2026)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution

- December 2026: a possible Commission proposal on laying hens and broilers, including an end to chick culling. Signals of delay are growing. A proposal would mostly affect expectations, not the 2027 number.
- 2027-01-01: Italy's ban takes effect. Watch for a last-minute postponement or funding from the budget law. The effect on an early or mid-2027 figure would be partial because of the 18-month turnover.
- Late 2026 to early 2027: Omegga/CET launch and other capacity additions.
- Ongoing: the HPAI season, which could change flock size and restocking.
- Around 2027-01: IAA's yearly recap. The 2025 recap came out 2026-01-04.
- 2027-03/04 and 2027-06/07: IAA quarterly roundups.
- The main 2027 report probably comes out between May and July 2027, possibly after the resolution date. Its measurement date (Q1 versus June) and any denominator revision both matter for resolution.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) The 2027 figure will probably be published around May to July 2027, so roughly 6 to 9 months from today (2026-11-05). The snapshot date is likely April or June 2027.

(b) The latest value is 40% of the EU commercial layer flock as of June 1, 2026 (range 36.2-43.3%), published by IAA in July 2026. The series has been revised onto a new flock basis: 23% in 2024, 34% in 2025, 40% in 2026.

(c) If nothing changed, the outcome would be about 40%.

(d) The recent trend is about +5 to 6 points per year, and IAA projects 51% by July 2028. Interpolating gives about 44-46% for a spring or mid-2027 snapshot. Italy's ban from January 2027 adds a little:
- Italy has about 40M hens, roughly 11% of the EU flock.
- Hatchery changes take about 20 weeks to reach the laying flock, so the ban likely adds only about 1-2 points by mid-2027.

(e) Year-over-year moves have been +6 to +11 points. Methodology revisions have moved past figures by 3 to 6 points, always upward so far. IAA's published uncertainty band is about ±3.5 points.

(f) No markets cover this. The only expert forecast is IAA's own path (51% by mid-2028, range 47-55%), which implies about 44-46% in 2027.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- Low: another flock-size revision, this time downward on the sexed side, plus the following, could hold the figure at about 36-39%.
  - Italian producers stall the ban or import unsexed chicks under extensions.
  - Avian influenza disrupts hatcheries.
  - A sexing provider has capacity problems.
- High: the figure could reach 52% or more if both of these happen:
  - Italy complies quickly through imported sexed chicks, and Spain and Poland adopt faster.
  - IAA revises upward again, or uses a later snapshot date.

- **High:** IAA makes another upward methodological revision, or Italy and other countries adopt faster than expected, with the Spanish and Polish hatchery capacity ramping up. The figure would then be above 50%.

(b) **Latest known value:** 40% (range 36.2-43.3%) as of June 1, 2026, published July 2026. The earlier series was revised upward: 23% in April 2024 and 34% in April 2025.

(c) **If nothing changed:** 40%. This is also the figure most likely to be restated in IAA's January 2027 year-in-review, which a resolver might treat as the "first number published in 2027".

(d) **If the trend continued:** The recent pace is about +5 points a year. IAA's path to about 51% by July 2028 implies roughly 44-45% for a snapshot in spring or summer 2027. Italy's ban from January 2027 adds only a little by mid-2027, because hens live about 80 weeks and the flock turns over slowly.

(e) **Historical variation:** The series has risen by 5-11 points a year. Methodology revisions have moved figures by 3-6 points, and the published uncertainty band is about ±3.5 points.

(f) **Expert and market expectations:** IAA forecasts about 51% by July 2028. No prediction market covers this question. Interpolating IAA's path gives about 43-45% for 2027.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** The flock-basis estimate is revised up again, or bird-flu culls hit flocks unevenly. Hatchery machines in Germany or France are idled because sexed eggs carry a cost premium, and Italy relies on importing sexed chicks or delays its ban. The share could then stall or dip to about 36-38%.
- **High:** Italy adopts quickly, a Commission proposal to end chick culling EU-wide drives early adoption, and another methodological revision pushes the figure to about 50% or more.
